acquirer-disclosure.title: Account and provider responsibilities
paragraphs: Etail provides the merchant services and support described in your agreement. The acquiring bank and other providers are responsible for the services covered by their agreements. Your account documents identify the payment methods, responsible providers and instructions you must follow.

The merchant remains responsible for its sales, customer obligations, authorized transaction submissions and applicable security and network requirements. Etail is not a bank. A payment facilitator relationship does not itself create a bank deposit, lending facility or deposit insurance coverage.

Accepting documents or opening account access does not activate processing. The responsible provider must confirm activation. Funding, reserves and recovery remain governed by the accepted account documents and required separate authorizations.

You must be told who receives transaction instructions, initiates payouts, holds reserves and collects amounts owed, together with the applicable authority and service contact. Each party acts only within its own assigned role. Required approvals and separate authorizations must be completed before the affected function is used.

acquirer-disclosure.title: Applicable acquirer terms
paragraphs: Obtain and retain the provider terms supplied for your account before accepting them. The account’s registration, processing scope and applicable network requirements determine which documents are needed and when they take effect. Complete any required acceptance or registration before processing that requires it, and preserve the document versions and acceptance record.

This disclosure identifies the bank; it is not the bank’s contract and does not create or amend rights on its behalf. Only the applicable provider can supply or authorize its operative terms. Questions about those documents should identify the merchant account and service involved.

Where a direct acquiring agreement or registration is required, complete it within the applicable network and acquiring deadline. Your account documents must identify the accepted card categories, any permitted choice to limit card acceptance, the bank contact and payment terms. This disclosure adds no fee and does not replace your accepted fee schedule.

Acceptance of Etail’s terms does not by itself accept a separate bank agreement or authorize Etail to change the bank’s obligations. Mandatory acquiring or network requirements govern the activities to which they apply. If a required provider agreement is absent or inconsistent with your instructions, do not begin the affected processing until the responsible provider resolves it.

acquirer-disclosure.title: Network requirements
paragraphs: Follow the applicable card network rules and acquiring instructions for the accepted methods, customer disclosures, transaction handling, security and disputes. A network or acquirer may require a service restriction or cessation within its lawful authority.

The Visa rules have geographic and product specific scope. An account agreement and current acquiring instructions provide requirements beyond the public overview. The reference below is not an endorsement or certification of Etail.

acquirer-disclosure.title: Notices and contact
paragraphs: Send legal notices and questions to compliance@etaildepot.com or Etail Depot US, Inc., 2001 L Street NW, Suite 500, Washington DC 20036, United States. Identify your business, service and the document concerned. Do not send identity documents, passwords or complete bank or card numbers by ordinary email.

merchant-privacy.title: Who this notice covers
paragraphs: This notice addresses personal information handled by Etail Depot US, Inc. in connection with United States merchant applications, account support and payment services. It covers business representatives, owners and other individuals whose information is involved. It does not make a customer’s purchase subject to the merchant’s business contract.

Website browsing is covered by the Website Privacy Policy. A bank, gateway or other provider may handle information for its own purposes under its own notice. This notice describes Etail’s role and does not replace those notices.

merchant-privacy.title: Information we handle
paragraphs: Etail staff can access application documents, owner identity information and bank information in the provider system. Information available for a particular account depends on the application, enabled services and assigned permissions.
bullets: Business and contact information, including names, addresses, roles and contact details.
Application and verification information supplied for the business and its owners or representatives, which may include identity documents and tax identifiers.
Bank information used for the merchant account and its approved funding arrangements.
Transaction references, amounts, statuses, adjustments and support correspondence available for the service.
Records of account instructions, authorizations, requests and service communications.

merchant-privacy.title: Where information comes from
paragraphs: Information may come from you and your representatives, the account service, service providers or an authorized software platform. Information you share in a support request becomes part of that request. We may view information in the provider system without downloading it.
Do not send sensitive application documents or complete payment credentials by ordinary email. Use the secure channel designated for the request.

merchant-privacy.title: How we use information
paragraphs: We use information to review and support applications, verify the authority of account contacts, provide your merchant services, investigate transaction or funding questions, communicate about your account and respond to privacy or legal requests.

Information may also be needed for fraud and security controls, applicable legal or network requirements, records of acceptance and resolution of disputes. The purpose and responsible party depend on the activity. Access for account support is not permission for unrelated marketing.

merchant-privacy.title: Service relationships and sharing
paragraphs: Information necessary for an account or transaction may be shared with the responsible acquiring bank, processing and verification providers, participating payment networks, and a software platform acting under the merchant’s authorization. Legal or security disclosures depend on the applicable obligation. Only information needed for the relevant purpose should be provided.

If you enroll in optional dispute prevention, Order Insight shares supported merchant, transaction and order information with participating banks. Eligibility, notices and permissions apply. Reading this notice does not enroll you in the service.

Banks and payment networks may handle information independently under their own privacy notices. Processing and access locations vary by provider and service. Contact us for the recipients and access arrangements applicable to your account.

merchant-privacy.title: Retention and security
paragraphs: How long we retain information depends on its purpose, the type of record, account obligations, unresolved claims and legal requirements. This includes records from closed accounts and abandoned applications. Account closure does not automatically erase required records. Retained information remains protected. Contact compliance@etaildepot.com to ask about a record’s retention, the applicable criteria or the available deletion process.

Access and disclosure must be limited to authorized purposes and appropriate roles. Use the designated secure account channel and keep your credentials private. No transmission or storage method can guarantee complete security.

merchant-privacy.title: Privacy requests and choices
paragraphs: Contact compliance@etaildepot.com without signing in. Identify the service, your relationship to the account and your request. Depending on applicable law, you may request confirmation, access, a portable copy, correction, deletion or limits on sensitive information use. Rights concerning sale, advertising or profiling apply where the relevant law and activity apply.

An authorized agent may act where permitted. We may verify identity and authority using information reasonably necessary for the request and arrange a secure channel for documents. Do not send identity documents, passwords or complete account numbers in the initial email.

We will respond within the applicable legal period and explain any permitted extension or refusal. To seek a review or an available appeal, email compliance@etaildepot.com with the subject Privacy appeal and the original request reference. We will explain the outcome and any available external complaint route. We will not unlawfully discriminate against you for exercising privacy rights.

Where consent is the basis for processing, you may withdraw it for future processing, subject to law. Withdrawal does not invalidate earlier lawful processing. Required records and lawful duties may continue. This notice does not itself authorize advertising, sale or unrelated use of personal information.

data-processing.title: 1. When these terms apply
paragraphs: These Data Processing Terms apply between Etail Depot US, Inc. and the merchant or software platform that expressly incorporates them into an accepted Service Order. They govern only the identified processing activities. They do not replace the privacy notice owed to an individual.

Before Etail processes personal information on your behalf, the Service Order or another record accepted by both parties must identify the purposes and duration, categories of information and people, each party’s responsibilities, authorized recipients, access locations, safeguards, retention and return or deletion. This processing record forms part of these terms and limits the processing to the activities it describes.

Personal information means information about an identified or identifiable person, as well as information protected as personal information under applicable law. Processing includes viewing information in a provider system and collecting, storing, using, sharing or deleting it. Each party’s responsibilities depend on its role in the agreed processing. Access to information alone does not make every provider Etail’s processor.

Etail staff can access merchant application documents, owner identity information and bank information in the provider system. That access does not itself authorize downloads, bank changes, consumer reports or other services.

data-processing.title: 2. Responsibilities and instructions
paragraphs: Each party’s role depends on how it uses personal information and on applicable law. Etail follows the customer’s documented instructions for processing carried out on the customer’s behalf. A party that decides independently why information is used must have its own lawful basis and provide the required privacy notice.
The customer must have authority to provide the information and instructions. Neither party may use these terms to avoid its own statutory responsibilities.

When Etail processes information solely on a customer’s instructions, the customer is the controller or business and Etail is its processor or service provider, as applicable. The processing record must describe the agreed tasks, such as checking an application for completeness, making requested corrections or responding to account questions.

If Etail reasonably believes an instruction violates applicable law, it must notify the customer and suspend that instruction while the concern is resolved. If law requires other processing, Etail must notify the customer before acting unless notice is prohibited. Any compulsory disclosure must be limited to what is required and its legal basis documented. Each party remains responsible for the notices and authority required for its own activities.

data-processing.title: 3. Purpose limits and confidentiality
paragraphs: Process information only for the recorded services, valid instructions or a legal duty. A legal requirement outside the instructions must be communicated where permitted. Restrict access to authorized people with a legitimate role and confidentiality obligations.

Review permissions when responsibilities change and remove access no longer needed. Exports, remote access and disclosures require a permitted purpose and appropriate controls. Do not copy customer information into unapproved personal accounts, public sharing locations or unrelated automated tools.

These terms do not authorize unrelated advertising, sale, biometric identification, unrestricted profiling or model training. A provider’s independent purposes must be described under its own role and governing terms; those purposes do not grant Etail equivalent use rights.

data-processing.title: 4. United States privacy requirements
paragraphs: Where United States state privacy law applies and Etail acts as a processor, service provider or contractor, Etail acknowledges and agrees to comply with the duties attached to that role. The processing record must state the specific permitted business purposes.

Etail must not sell or share covered information as those terms are defined by the applicable law. Use, retention and disclosure are limited to those purposes and the direct service relationship, except as law permits. Combining covered information with other records is prohibited unless the applicable law allows it.

Etail must provide the protection required by that law and notify the customer if it determines that it cannot meet these obligations. The customer may take reasonable and appropriate steps to verify compliance and, upon notice, stop and remedy unauthorized use. Etail must assist with applicable individual requests. These duties also apply through written terms to processors Etail appoints for the covered work.

Where required, Etail certifies that it understands and will comply with the restrictions applicable to its role. Assistance includes applicable audits, risk assessments and automated decision requirements. A legal exemption applies only to the information and activity it covers; use of a financial provider does not exempt every account record.

data-processing.title: 5. Security and incidents
paragraphs: Each party must implement and maintain safeguards appropriate to the information and its responsibilities, document those safeguards and require appropriate protection from people acting for it. The processing record must identify access controls, secure transmission and storage, incident handling and deletion arrangements.

A covered incident is an actual loss, unauthorized access, use, disclosure, alteration or destruction of the personal information governed by these terms. Investigation and notification duties apply to affected information within the party’s responsibility, including its appointed processors.

Notify the other party without undue delay after becoming aware of an incident affecting the covered information, subject to applicable law and any stricter agreed deadline. Provide available details about affected information, likely impact, investigation and mitigation, with further updates as information becomes available. Responsibility for regulatory and individual notices follows applicable law.

Each party must maintain a written security program appropriate to its activities and information risk. For Etail access, agreed safeguards must cover individual accounts, restricted permissions, multifactor authentication, protected devices, encrypted transmission and storage, access records, staff instruction, incident response and disposal. Any alternative must be documented, lawful and provide appropriate protection. Provider controls do not replace safeguards for Etail staff, devices or exports.

The processing record must describe the safeguards in place, who operates them and how they are checked. Etail must assess providers entrusted with information and require suitable written safeguards. A provider’s certification does not certify Etail’s systems or practices.

An initial incident notice must not wait for a complete investigation. Cooperate on containment, evidence preservation, recovery and required notices. Notification or cooperation is not an admission of fault. Costs follow responsibility and the accepted agreement, not an automatic charge to the customer.

data-processing.title: 6. Service providers and locations
paragraphs: Provider changes must follow the process in the agreed processing record. Etail must require equivalent privacy and security duties in its written contracts with appointed processors. Etail remains responsible to the customer for their covered processing as if Etail performed it itself, subject to the accepted service agreement and applicable law.

Etail must give at least 30 days’ advance notice before adding or replacing a processor it appoints, unless an urgent lawful requirement prevents that period. The customer may raise a reasonable data protection objection. The parties must resolve it or lawfully end the affected processing before the change where required. Independently acting banks and networks do not become Etail’s subprocessors under this clause.

Access outside the United States requires a lawful arrangement and any required notice or transfer measures. The processing record must identify the countries in which information may be stored or accessed.

For each authorized recipient, the processing record must identify its legal entity, who appoints it, its function and role, the information it can access, and the countries where it stores or accesses information. Etail must have written protection terms in place before an appointed processor receives information processed on the customer’s instructions. Linking to a provider’s public terms does not make that provider a party to this agreement or release Etail from its duties.

Any provider change procedure that differs from these terms must be expressly addressed in the agreement before acceptance. Services for United States merchants may involve access or storage outside the United States. Required transfer safeguards must cover the parties and processing involved; a provider’s certification or legal status does not extend to Etail.

data-processing.title: 7. Requests and cooperation
paragraphs: Etail must promptly forward privacy requests about information it processes on the customer’s instructions to that customer, unless law requires a direct response. Each party must provide reasonable assistance with requests, security inquiries and legally required assessments using information within its control.

Respond lawfully to government requests. Limit disclosure and notify the other party where permitted. Reasonable evidence of compliance may be supplied through documentation and agreed review arrangements without exposing another customer’s confidential information or weakening security.

For information processed on a customer’s instructions, Etail may verify a requester’s identity or direct the request to the customer. Etail must not decide the customer’s response without lawful instructions, except as law requires. Etail handles requests about information it uses for its own purposes. Verification must protect other people’s information.

A confidentiality or audit restriction cannot defeat a legal obligation to provide further inspection or corrective action. Protect other customers’ records while supplying the evidence reasonably needed for a lawful, proportionate review.

data-processing.title: 8. Return and deletion
paragraphs: When processing ends, Etail must return or delete information in accordance with the processing record and the customer’s lawful instructions, except for information required for a continuing obligation or legal retention. Etail must identify any retained categories, their purpose and access restrictions. Backups follow the documented deletion cycle. Retained information, including backups, remains protected after the service ends and until deletion, with access limited to the purpose requiring retention.

For each category of information, the parties must agree on a retention period or a measurable condition for deletion, the legal or service reason for retention, a review date and the deletion method. Each party must keep only the information needed for that purpose, document any legal hold and limit use accordingly. Identity and bank documents must not be kept indefinitely simply because they were once accessible.

The processing record must specify the format for returning information, the time allowed for return or deletion and the backup deletion cycle. Etail must document completion and any permitted exception. Removing account access does not delete the information. Independently acting recipients remain responsible for their own lawful retention.

data-processing.title: 9. Relationship to the service agreement
paragraphs: These terms control the covered data processing if inconsistent with general service wording, subject to mandatory law. Fees, funding, liability and dispute resolution remain in the accepted Service Order and service terms unless expressly amended.
Only provider documents expressly incorporated into the accepted service agreement form part of this processing arrangement.

data-processing.title: 10. Your data processing arrangements
paragraphs: The processing record may be included in your Service Order or supplied as a separate schedule. Both parties must receive and accept it before the covered processing begins. It limits the purposes, information and activities covered. Changes require documentation and acceptance where applicable.

Access within a provider system does not by itself permit downloads, separate storage or onward disclosure. The agreed arrangements must describe actual safeguards and retention. An activity, recipient, location or use that has not been authorized is not permitted merely because account access is available.

security-policy.title: Shared security responsibilities
paragraphs: Each party is responsible for the security of the services and systems it controls. You are responsible for your website, devices, user access and handling of payment information. Etail is responsible for the safeguards and duties set out in its agreement. Providers retain their own responsibilities.
Each party must meet the security and validation requirements applicable to the systems it controls. Request current validation documents for the services and systems within your responsibility.

security-policy.title: Protect account access
paragraphs: Give each authorized person only the access required for their role. Keep credentials and verification codes private, use available account protection features and remove access when a person no longer needs it.
Verify bank changes and unusual instructions through the designated secure process. Do not send passwords or complete bank details in a support email. Report suspected unauthorized access promptly.

security-policy.title: Handle payment information safely
paragraphs: Use the approved checkout and payment entry methods. PCI DSS requirements depend on the environment and the account’s validation obligations. A hosted checkout can reduce exposure but does not remove all merchant responsibilities.

Do not retain card verification codes, full magnetic stripe or equivalent chip track data, PINs or PIN blocks after authorization, even if encrypted. Keep payment credentials out of logs, analytics, support messages and ordinary email. Minimize other stored information and protect it under the applicable requirements.

security-policy.title: Your website and integration
paragraphs: Maintain supported software, protect integration credentials, limit access and review changes that can affect checkout or customer information. Confirm payment and refund status before retrying an uncertain request. Preserve useful references without placing sensitive information in records.
Follow the integration and security instructions supplied for your account. Obtain current documentation from your integration contact before enabling a new function.
For systems and information each party controls, its documented safeguards must address the following in proportion to the information and risks involved:
bullets: Individual access permissions, suitable authentication, periodic access review and prompt removal of unnecessary access.
Secure transmission and storage, with encryption and control of keys where appropriate to the information and risk.
Supported software, security updates, review of vulnerabilities and monitoring for unauthorized activity.
Staff confidentiality duties, security awareness and restrictions on unnecessary copies or exports.
Incident response, protected recovery arrangements where information is stored, and secure disposal at the end of retention.

security-policy.title: Report an incident
paragraphs: Contact compliance@etaildepot.com with the affected service, approximate time and a brief description. Do not include passwords, complete card numbers, bank credentials or customer files in the first message. We will identify an appropriate channel for further information.

Take reasonable steps within your control to contain the issue and preserve relevant evidence. Follow the incident process and notice duties in the account and provider agreements. A routine report does not authorize access to another person’s systems or data.

security-policy.title: Security documentation
paragraphs: Request current security and responsibility information for the services in your account, including the service scope, document version and issuing organization.
